title: Angles: Measuring, Drawing and Angles in a Triangle
kicker: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint · Mathematics · Stage 6 · Geometry and Measure
summary: Classify, estimate, measure and draw angles with a protractor, and use the fact that the angles in a triangle add up to 180°.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex; estimate the size of an angle; measure angles with a protractor; and draw angles of a given size. [6Gg.09]
Know that the three angles in any triangle add up to 180°, and use this to calculate a missing angle in a triangle. [6Gg.10]

blocks.text: An **angle** measures an amount of turn between two lines (arms) that meet at a point (the vertex). We measure angles in **degrees (°)**. A full turn is 360°, half a turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°. On this page you will learn to name, estimate, measure and draw angles, and then use the most important angle fact of Stage 6: **the angles in a triangle add up to 180°**.
1. Key words

items: angle
زاوية — the amount of turn between two arms
vertex
رأس الزاوية — the point where the two arms meet
degree (°)
درجة — the unit for measuring angles
acute angle
زاوية حادة — less than 90°

زاوية قائمة — exactly 90°
obtuse angle

blocks.text: **Estimating.** Compare the angle with a right angle (90°) and a straight line (180°). Half a right angle is 45°; a right angle split into three gives 30° and 60°. For example, an angle a little bigger than a right angle might be about 100°; an angle about halfway between a right angle and a straight line is about 135°. Always estimate before you measure — it stops you reading the wrong scale.

items: **Estimate first**: is the angle acute or obtuse?
Put the centre point (cross) of the protractor exactly on the **vertex**.
Turn the protractor so that the 0° line lies exactly along **one arm** (the baseline).
Find the scale that starts at **0** on that arm. Follow THAT scale round to the other arm.
Read the number where the second arm crosses the scale. If the arm is short, extend it with a ruler first.
Check against your estimate: an acute angle cannot read 130°.

blocks.text: A protractor has two scales because the angle can open to the right or to the left. In the diagram above, the arm on the right sits on 0 of the inner (blue) scale, so the inner scale gives the answer: 50°. The outer scale shows 130° at the same place — that is 180° − 50°, the angle on the other side.
4. Measuring a reflex angle
A semicircular protractor only goes up to 180°, so measure the smaller angle and subtract from 360°.

blocks.text: 5. Drawing an angle of a given size
**To draw an angle of 70° at point A:**

items: Draw a straight line (the first arm) with a ruler, and mark the vertex A at one end.
Place the protractor's centre on A with the 0° line along your arm.
Using the scale that starts at 0 on your arm, count round to 70 and make a small dot.
Remove the protractor and join A to the dot with a ruler.
Mark the angle with an arc and write 70°. Check it looks acute!

blocks.text: **To draw a reflex angle such as 250°:** work out 360° − 250° = 110°, draw an angle of 110°, then mark the OUTSIDE angle with an arc and label it 250°.

blocks.title: المنقلة بالخطوات
items: حط مركز المنقلة على رأس الزاوية بالظبط، وخلي خط الصفر على أحد الضلعين.
اقرأ من التدريج اللي بيبدأ بصفر عند الضلع ده — مش من التدريج التاني.
قدّر الأول: لو الزاوية حادة يبقى الإجابة أقل من 90°.

blocks.text: 6. The angles in a triangle add up to 180°
Draw any triangle on paper, colour its three corners, tear them off and put them together at one point. They always fit exactly on a straight line — and a straight line is 180°.

blocks.text: **To find a missing angle in a triangle:** add the angles you know, then subtract the total from 180°.

headers: How to find the missing angles
rows: the other two add up to 90°, so missing angle = 90° − known angle
the two base angles are equal
if you know the top angle: (180° − top) ÷ 2; if you know a base angle: 180° − 2 × base

blocks.text: Two facts that follow: a triangle can have **at most one** right angle or obtuse angle (two of them would already make 180° or more), and every triangle has **at least two** acute angles.

blocks.title: أهم قاعدة
items: مجموع زوايا أي مثلث = 180°. اجمع الزاويتين المعروفتين واطرحهم من 180°.
المثلث متساوي الساقين: زاويتين القاعدة متساويتين. المثلث متساوي الأضلاع: كل زاوية 60°.

blocks.text: 7. Worked examples

**Worked example 1** (1 mark)
Write each angle in the correct column: 118°, 90°, 44°, 270°, 180°, 89°.
Common mistake: putting 89° with the right angles. 89° is less than 90°, so it is acute — even though it looks almost square.

**Worked example 2** (1 mark)
Use the protractor diagram in section 3. What is the size of the angle?

items: Estimate: the angle is clearly acute, so the answer is less than 90°.
The baseline (right arm) is on 0 of the inner scale, so use the inner scale.
The other arm crosses the inner scale at 50.
**Answer: 50°.** (130° would be wrong — it is obtuse.)

blocks.text:
**Worked example 3** (1 mark)
The diagram shows a triangle. Work out the size of angle a.

blocks.caption: Triangle with angles 65° and 40° (drawn to scale).

items: Add the known angles: 65° + 40° = 105°.

blocks.text:
**Worked example 4** (2 marks)
An isosceles triangle has one angle of 52°. The other two angles are equal to each other. Find them.

items: The 52° angle is the different one, so the two equal angles share 180° − 52° = 128°.
Each equal angle = 128° ÷ 2 = 64°.
Marks: 1 mark for 180 − 52 (or 128 seen), 1 mark for 64°.

blocks.text: Watch the wording: if the question says the 52° angle is one of the two EQUAL angles, then the angles are 52°, 52° and 180° − 104° = 76°. Read carefully which angle is repeated.

**Worked example 5** (1 mark)
A right-angled triangle has one angle of 27°. What is the third angle?

items: The right angle is 90°, so the other two angles add up to 180° − 90° = 90°.
Third angle = 90° − 27° = 63°.
**Answer: 63°.**

blocks.text:
**Worked example 6** (1 mark)
Omar measured the angles of a triangle and got 64°, 71° and 55°. Explain how you know he has made a mistake.
**Answer:** 64 + 71 + 55 = 190°, but the angles in a triangle must add up to 180°. So at least one measurement is wrong (they are 10° too much altogether).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Reading the wrong protractor scale — e.g. writing 130° for an acute angle. Always estimate first.
Putting the protractor's edge, not its centre point, on the vertex.
Not lining up the 0° line exactly along the arm.
Forgetting that a reflex angle is the OUTSIDE angle: measure the inside angle and subtract from 360°.
Adding the angles and forgetting to subtract from 180° (giving 105° instead of 75°).
In an isosceles triangle, not checking which angle is repeated.
Using 360° for a triangle (360° is a full turn — and the angle sum of a quadrilateral — not of a triangle).

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: Ring or tick the correct name (acute, obtuse, reflex…) or sort angles into a table.
Estimate: "Which is the best estimate of this angle?" — compare with 90° and 180°.
Measure an angle printed on the paper with your protractor. The angle is drawn accurately, so measure carefully and extend short arms with a ruler.
Draw an angle of a given size from a line already drawn on the paper.
Calculate a missing angle in a triangle. Diagrams are often marked "not drawn to scale" — then you must calculate, not measure.
Explain why something is impossible, e.g. a triangle with two obtuse angles or angles that add to more than 180°.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Angles — practice quiz
blocks.intro: 14 questions. The angles in the pictures are drawn accurately, so you can check your estimates with a protractor. Have a ruler and protractor ready for the last question and mark it yourself.

questions.e: 135° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

questions.q: Which of these angles is a reflex angle?
questions.e: A reflex angle is between 180° and 360°. Only 205° is in that range. 180° is a straight angle; 95° and 175° are obtuse.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate of the size of this angle?
questions.e: The angle is much smaller than a right angle (90°) and less than half of one is 45°, so it is acute and about 35°. (It is drawn accurately — you can check with a protractor.)

questions.q: This is a right-angled triangle. Work out angle y.
questions.e: The right angle is 90°, so the other two angles add up to 90°. y = 90° − 34° = 56°.

questions.q: What is the size of each angle in an equilateral triangle?
questions.e: All three angles are equal and add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

questions.q: The angle marked 110° is shown. What is the size of the reflex angle r?
questions.e: The reflex angle and the 110° angle make a full turn. r = 360° − 110° = 250°.

questions.q: Which set of three angles could be the angles of a triangle?
questions.e: Only 100 + 50 + 30 = 180. The others add up to 190°, 190° and 135°.

questions.q: In a triangle, two angles are equal and the third angle is 100°. What is the size of each of the equal angles?
questions.e: 180° − 100° = 80°. The two equal angles share 80°, so each is 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has two other angles that are equal. What size are they?
questions.e: The two equal angles add up to 180° − 90° = 90°, so each is 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.

questions.q: Mona says: "I drew a triangle with two obtuse angles." Explain why this is impossible.
questions.ms: 1 mark: explanation using the angle sum, e.g. two obtuse angles are each more than 90°, so together they are more than 180°, but all three angles of a triangle add up to only 180°. Do not accept "triangles can't have obtuse angles".
questions.e: Each obtuse angle is more than 90°, so two of them add up to more than 180°. But the three angles of a triangle add up to exactly 180°, so there is nothing left for the third angle. A triangle can have at most one obtuse angle.

questions.q: Draw a line AB 6 cm long. At A, draw an angle of 125°. Label the angle. Then extend the line BA beyond A with a ruler. Measure the angle between this extension and your new arm, and check that the two angles add up to 180°.
questions.ms: 1 mark: angle at A drawn between 123° and 127° using a protractor, with the arm drawn with a ruler and the angle labelled 125°. 1 mark: the angle between the extension of BA and the arm measured as 55° (accept 53°–57°). Do not accept an acute angle drawn by reading the wrong scale.
questions.e: Put the protractor centre on A with 0° along AB. Using the scale that starts at 0 on AB, count to 125 and mark a dot; join it to A. The angle is obtuse — check it opens wider than a right angle. Extending BA past A makes a straight line, and the angle on the other side is 180° − 125° = 55°.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Acute < 90° · right = 90° · obtuse between 90° and 180° · straight = 180° · reflex between 180° and 360°.
Protractor: centre on the vertex, 0° along one arm, read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm. Estimate first!
Reflex angle = 360° − the smaller angle.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°: missing angle = 180° − (the other two).
Equilateral: 60° each. Isosceles: two equal base angles. Right-angled: the other two angles add up to 90°.
